rows.detail: R1/R2 both pass mechanically (large real matrix, ubuntu-latest+node-22 cells present and green in recent completed runs), but the job's actual Node-version matrix is computed at runtime by a third-party reusable action (ljharb/actions/node/matrix@main) and its install step is another reusable action (ljharb/actions/node/install@main) - neither's real behavior is stated in this repository's own workflow YAML. Hand-transcribing 'the exact command this cell runs' would require reverse-engineering an external actions repository, which is exactly the kind of human command repair the reference-plan discipline forbids. Not evaluated against R3 - rejected before that step, on legibility of the workflow itself, not on any expectation about outcome.

R1/R2/R4 all passed (see below); reference plan hand-transcribed and frozen (docs/evidence/ci-reproduction-05-rimraf-reference-plan.json) BEFORE running R3. R3 result: R3_FAILED - 'the reference arm executed no suite, so there is nothing to reproduce'. This is not a transcription error: both commands ran exactly as the workflow states them, both exited 0, and the real underlying test run genuinely executed and passed (17/17 suites, 782/782 asserts - visible in the raw outputTail, docs/evidence/external-engine-bridge-01-first-pilot-screening/rimraf-r3-failed.json). The cause is that rimraf's test script invokes node-tap's own CLI reporter, whose pretty-printed summary format ('Asserts: N pass', 'Suites: N pass', a decorative TEST COMPLETE banner) is not one the harness's evidence parser currently recognizes as a completed suite - a real, structural harness limitation, distinct in kind from eslint's dependency-pinning gap. Per protocol this is evidence, not something to patch around (extending the parser to recognize a new reporter format is new engine scope, out of bounds for this pilot) - rejected, moving to the next rank.
